title: Adani Group Unveils $120 Billion Capex Plan Over Five Years
headline: Adani Group Unveils $120 Billion Capex Plan Over Five Years
subheadline: Executives told Fortune India the group plans more than $20 billion a year across energy, transport and adjacencies — a group-wide five-year plan distinct from Adani Enterprises' annual guidance last week.
summary: Executives told Fortune India the group plans more than $20 billion a year across energy, transport and adjacencies — a group-wide five-year plan distinct from Adani Enterprises' annual guidance last week.
excerpt: Executives told Fortune India the group plans more than $20 billion a year across energy, transport and adjacencies — a group-wide five-year plan distinct from Adani Enterprises' annual guidance last week.
body:
• Adani Group executives told Fortune India they plan to invest about $120 billion in capital expenditure over the next five years — more than $20 billion a year — across all group businesses.
  • About 70% is earmarked for energy, about 20% for transport and logistics, and 10% for adjacencies such as cement, copper and aluminium, according to Reuters reporting of the interview.
  • This is a group-wide, five-year plan, distinct from Adani Enterprises' separate guidance last week of Rs 35,000–40,000 crore a year for the next couple of years for that one flagship company alone.
  • For diaspora investors, the figures are a plan, not a result: the group estimates the spending would double its asset base to Rs 18 lakh crore and lift core earnings to Rs 2.6–3 lakh crore in five years.

India's Adani Group plans to invest more than $120 billion in capital expenditure over the next five years across its core infrastructure businesses and emerging growth platforms, its executives told Fortune India in an interview on Tuesday, according to Reuters.

"Over the next five years, we plan to invest about $120 billion — over $20 billion a year — across all our businesses."

— Pranav Adani, Director, Adani Enterprises, told Fortune India

Pranav Adani is a director at the group's flagship firm Adani Enterprises and the nephew of group chairman Gautam Adani, Reuters said. The group did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

Where the money would go

Broadly, about 70% of the investments will be in energy, about 20% in transport and logistics and 10% in business adjacencies such as cement, copper and aluminium, the Reuters report in The Hindu BusinessLine said. A second report carried by TradingView gave the same split and the same five-year totals.

The group has businesses spanning ports, airports, power and renewable energy. Those are the sectors the new plan covers, alongside the newer adjacencies named above. The reports do not break the $120 billion down project by project, and no project-level timetable was given in the interview excerpts published by Reuters.

How this differs from last week's Adani Enterprises guidance

This is not a restatement of the annual figure already reported. Last week Adani Enterprises — one listed company within the group — said on its earnings call that it expected capex at a run rate of Rs 35,000 crore to Rs 40,000 crore a year over the next couple of years, led by airports, data centres and its Mundra PVC complex. We covered that guidance separately in Adani Enterprises Plans Rs 35,000-40,000 Crore Annual Capex Over Next Two Years. That same reporting put the flagship's first-half EBITDA at a record Rs 11,958 crore, up 56% from a year earlier.

The Fortune India plan is larger in scope and in horizon: it covers all group businesses, not only Adani Enterprises, runs over five years rather than the next couple, and is stated in dollars at more than $20 billion a year for the group as a whole. The Enterprises run rate sits inside that wider group picture rather than replacing it.

What the group says it would produce

The report said the group estimates these investments will help double its asset base to Rs 18 lakh crore ($191.64 billion) and generate core earnings, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, of Rs 2.6 lakh crore to Rs 3 lakh crore in five years. Those are the group's own estimates for what the plan could deliver. They are guidance, not reported performance, and they depend on projects being financed and built on schedule.

What to watch next

For investors — including diaspora holders of Adani's listed companies — the next evidence will be company-level spending: whether Adani Enterprises holds its stated run rate, how the energy and transport companies sequence their own capex, and whether asset and earnings growth tracks the five-year estimates the executives gave Fortune India. Until filings and results confirm the pace, the $120 billion figure should be read as an announced plan.
